messages:
anya: Heads-up — I’m seeing a big spike in late telemetry that’s ballooned the recompute backlog (~4k day-partitions). This started after the retry-window tweak yesterday. Anyone else?

matt: I’m seeing the same. EU ingest lag + a bunch of small parquet files. Backfill jobs are queuing behind nightly runs. :eyes: 

jess: Is this the change that increased max-retries from 3->6? Could be duplicating events and causing more small files + compaction lag.

leon: Yes, that change increased fanout. Two quick ideas: 1) Prioritize user-facing aggregates (billing, DAU) for immediate recompute. 2) Run compaction on affected partitions before re-running aggregate recompute.

sasha: Proposal: add a priority windowing policy — high priority = last 48h, medium = 48h-7d, low = >7d. High gets immediate sloting; medium gets rate-limited; low runs as background. Also require idempotent recompute flag.

anya: Love the windowing idea. Also we should route heavy backfills to Dedicated pool when available so hosted API SLOs don’t regress. Can we make a routing policy that pins backfill jobs to dedicated if dedicated_capacity_pct > 15%?

matt: Yep. We have routing rule support already. Something like: `route.job(backfill).prefer(dedicated).when(dedicated.free_pct > 15).fallthrough=hosted`

leon: Also add concurrency caps per-region. Suggest max_concurrent_recomputes = 2 for EU until we clear compaction. 

jess: For safety, throttle runs that exceed 2h: auto-pause further medium jobs and alert on-call. We don’t want a long job to block everything.

anya: UX note — Console needs an affordance to: select priority bucket, estimate token/compute cost, and choose target pool (hosted/dedicated/private). We should show ETA and an estimated cost delta if routed to dedicated.

matt: I’ll prototype a small API change: POST /internal/backfill with body {start,end,priority,target_pool,concurrency_hint,tag}. Keep it internal for now.

jess: Can we include a dry-run mode that emits estimated row counts and bytes so console can show estimates? `?dry_run=true` -> returns stats.

leon: For the recompute job itself, run compaction first:

```
# compaction job (airflow task)
python airflow_tasks/compact_partitions.py \
  --dataset telemetry_events --partitions 2026-03-01..2026-03-07
```

then recompute:

```
spark-submit \
  --class com.redwood.telemetry.Recompute \
  --conf spark.executor.memory=32g \
  recompute.jar \
  --start 2026-03-01 --end 2026-03-07 --partition=day --idempotent
```

anya: Good. Make sure the recompute writes to temp path and does atomic swap to avoid partial reads by dashboards.

platform-bot: job 4672 queued (backfill: 2026-03-01..2026-03-07, priority=high) :gear:

jess: Quick safety checklist:
- idempotent flag on job :white_check_mark:
- temp-path + atomic-swap :white_check_mark:
- compaction scheduled :white_check_mark:
- circuit-breaker to stop if API p90 latency increases 20% :inbox_tray:

matt: On the routing side I’ll add the policy and a fallback to hosted after 30m of retry attempts. Also adding metric `backfill.running.count` and `backfill.queued.count` to telemetry so we can alert on build-ups.

anya: We should also add a console toggle to mark certain tags as high-priority automatically (ex: billing, compliance). Saves a ton of manual ops.

leon: One more operational note: when a backfill touches >100 partitions, break it into windowed jobs of 7 days each to avoid long runtime.

anya: Action items: 1) matt — add routing policy + metrics, 2) jess — add throttling/circuit-breaker + dry-run stats endpoint, 3) anya — console mock for priority buckets & estimate, 4) leon — compaction + windowing helper in airflow. I’ll DM owners and open a tiny RFC.

platform-bot: job 4672 started on dedicated-east (executor=4, ETA=3h)

jess: monitoring alerts hooked to `backfill.running.count` and API p90. Will pause medium jobs automatically if p90 > baseline * 1.2.

anya: Thanks all — let’s treat this as a small ops run for the next 24h. Post any odd failures here and we’ll re-evaluate tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
